acceptance_walk:
I ran the bench "review-l4-starts-sessions" (daemon 49150, UI 2750) from my worktree at b306883. I used the stand-in only and started it fresh 4 times. The walk JSONs, with every step's screen text, are in /tmp/frbench/review-l4-starts-sessions/walk1..7.json. Screenshots of walk 6 are in /tmp/frbench/review-l4-starts-sessions/kept-steps/. The later --fresh starts wiped the steps/ folder of walks 1-5, so their screen texts survive only in the JSONs.

Walk 1-2 (201), bench-api with --api-key refused. I pressed Start in the UI on "Field notes". The session stopped at once to wait. More > Sessions showed "1 session / Nothing finished. / 16:33 · under a minute · Stopped to wait for a Claude credential · CHF 0.00", and GET /projects/:id/sessions returned count 1. I saved an ok key through POST /setup/anthropic. The work then went on by itself. The tab showed 2 sessions; the newer row read "... · goes on with your session of 16:33". I restarted the daemon (restart-daemon.mjs) and both rows stayed, still with count 2. PASS.

Walk 3 (202/205/206/213), FORERUNNER_BENCH_ASK. Two questions cards appeared. Under Send answers: "The task goes on with your answers; it runs at your next Start." Go ahead without: "...; it runs at your next Start." I answered one card through the UI form. Nothing started. While a session of the project ran, the other card read "...; it joins the running session if it fits." With start_by_itself on (settings.set plus its yes), it read "...; a session starts for it by itself." The answer then started a session. Its page's first line was "Started by itself when work was ready (this project's setting), with a budget of CHF 5.00." and its row said "started by itself when work was ready". Once both tasks were done, the Answered lines were 'Answers saved in the decision record; "X" is done.'. The Sessions row went "2 needed you · 2 still need you", then "2 needed you · 1 still needs you". The session page badge still read "Ended: 1 task needs you". PASS.

Walk 4 (207/208). The header read 'The coder works on "Write the quote list in quotes.md" (0 of 2 done)', the same words as the bar. Last result read "Running now: Open the session". I crashed the daemon with restart-daemon --hard. Inbox > Updates showed the Update with Continue and "Opens Start with the rest of your last session and the CHF 5.00 left of its budget." The press opened the Start dialog ("What is left of that session's budget is filled in: it goes on with that, never more."). Its Start posted continues, both tasks finished, and the Continue then went away. PASS.

Walk 5 (209). While Club site ran, Start on Bird notes was queued. Its header read 'Starts after the session on "Club site"' with Cancel. There was no Start session button at 1280 or at 375 px, and no sideways scroll. A second POST /sessions answered queued with the same startId and 'A session of Bird notes already starts after the session on "Club site".'. Cancel dropped the start and Start session came back. PASS. My 203 try on the bench did not exercise the case: the CHF 0.03 session ended before Make ready. I verified 203 through its real-daemon case instead.

Walk 6 (208), bench-api with --api-key limited and a slow critic. The Overview at 1280 and 375 px had 2 Cancels: the bar's and Working now's, so exactly one outside the bar. The header line read "Waiting until 16:44 (your API key's limit), then it goes on" with no action, and there was no sideways scroll. After the reset, the session page's Current task read 'The critic checks "Write the legend in legend.md"' and the header read 'The critic checks "..." (0 of 1 done)'. PASS.

Walk 7 (207 sibling), on the stand-in. Crash, Continue, then Stop now on the continuation. The Update then offered Continue again with the full CHF 1.00. That is blocking item 2 below.

Tests. I ran the fixer's named tests on the fix branch: all pass. I then reverted the 23 modified source files to claude/nifty-knuth-f9udt0 and kept the new tests and the two new leaf modules. All 8 new or changed real-daemon cases failed with the expected assertions: Quit-during-review/207, 201, 202, 203, 204, 208, 209 and 213. 37 runtime, commands and state unit tests failed too, among them starts-words 205/202, event-lines 206, session-list 213, the state suite's 201 case, session-join too_large and the commands limitChanged case. I restored the sources and the worktree is clean.

Under the heavy lock: pnpm check passed (560 files, 6161 tests; links and secret scan clean). docs-check --base passed. The full UI vitest suite passed (103 files, 1494 tests), Playwright passed (40 tests, including the new 208 cases at 1280 and 375 px), and pnpm test:e2e passed (25). I stopped the bench and deleted its home.

blocking.issue: L4-money-214 is not built, and it is not on the area's cut line. The spec lists the items that may end in not_done: 210, 211, 212, 215, 216, 207's time half, 208's session-page and Last-result parts, and 202's Tasks-row tooltips and chat's option line. 214 is not among them and is sized Medium. Its acceptance line fails: a session whose only task the person paused still ends with the result 'CHF 0.01.' and nothing else. The L4f review treated non-cut items left unbuilt as blocking.

There is no 'You paused' builder anywhere in packages/runtime/src: grep finds only runner.ts:3924's pausedByYou helper, which removes the task from needsYou, and no LastSessionOutcome.pausedByYou. result.ts has the W15-59 'cancelled by you' line but none for 'paused by you'. The live check evidence is L4-l3-8 (l3b state.sqlite: summary 'CHF 0.01.', session.ended counts 0).
blocking.expected: Build what the triage note L4-132 asks for. Add LastSessionOutcome.pausedByYou. Add a line-2 builder beside 'cancelled by you': 'You paused "X"; nothing else ran.', then the money line. Append its sentence to NOT_NEWS, so there is no Inbox Update or notification. The status note must not say 'needs you'. sessionGist should read '"X" paused by you.' Add a composed case like continuity-cancel.test.ts:787 and a writing-rules unit case. blocking.issue: L4-money-207 sibling (validation rule 8, money rule 'never more', writing rule 4 'true now'): the crash Update keeps offering Continue after a later session of the project has begun. It offers the interrupted session's whole remaining budget again. The new crashContinueOf only checks that nothing of the project runs now and that a released task is ready. The session page's Continue, waitBlockOf in server.ts, already hides its Continue 'once a later session of its project began'.
blocking.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:982 (crashContinueOf); apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts (the same rule in the fake)
blocking.evidence: Bench walk 7, /tmp/frbench/review-l4-starts-sessions/walk7.json, on the stand-in. I started a CHF 1.00 session and hard-restarted the daemon while it ran. The Update read: Continue, 'Opens Start with the rest of your last session and the CHF 1.00 left of its budget.' I pressed it: POST /sessions with continues started a session capped at CHF 1.00. I pressed Stop now on that continuation, which had spent CHF 0.0034; its task went back to Ready. GET /inbox then offered the same Continue again: 'the CHF 1.00 left of its budget', sessionId = the interrupted session. The second POST /sessions with continues started another CHF 1.00 session. Two continuations of one interrupted CHF 1.00 session can together spend more than what was left. Meanwhile the Start dialog says 'it goes on with that, never more', and 'your last session' now names a session that is not the last one. The area spec's money rule says: 'The crash Continue goes on with what is left of the interrupted session's budget ... never more'.
blocking.expected: Offer the crash Update's Continue only while no later session of the project has begun since the interrupted one, as waitBlockOf does. With the press marking the Update read (the triage note asks for that too), the Update then keeps Mark read only. Keep the fake daemon's mirror in step. Add a real-daemon case next to the 'Quit during Being reviewed' case: Continue, stop the continuation, and GET /inbox offers no Continue.
